instructions: Template values are placeholders. Confirm actual image mode, measured chessboard square size and the physical camera/lens connection before capturing.

An example initial dataset could use image_size=[640,480] and a 9-by-6 inner-corner board with measured 20mm squares; these are examples only, not current camera or target measurements. Choose the supported forward ray-angle request separately after inspecting actual coverage.
Use native_camera_capture.py native PNG/raw RGB565/metadata records; the calibrator checks image SHA, metadata SHA, raw SHA/CRC, unmodified RGB565 pixels and declared identity.
Set provenance=real_sensor_captures only for current physical captures. UART replays remain offline/unverified and cannot become real-lens ready.
Copy view_template to views, assigning every image a view_id, global physical pose_id and session_id. Choose split=train, model_selection or held_out explicitly before fitting.
Provide at least 12 distinct training poses and 3 separate held_out poses; collect many more views spanning the required source-image cells and edges for independent acceptance.

Only train views fit K/D. Model_selection views may review the fixed model but are never refitted; all train and model_selection hashes are included in calibration_image_sha256 for downstream stereo leakage checks.
A pose cannot occur in held_out and train/model_selection even under different filenames. Identical hashes and near-identical held-out corner poses are rejected.
All metadata identity_binding fields must exactly match camera_id/lens_id/profile_id/capture_mode_id; hashes bind an operator-declared connection and do not independently prove sensor/eye identity.

maximum_ray_angle_deg is an engineering domain request, not a measured lens FOV. It must remain below 90 degrees. The current OpenCV forward model cannot certify a seller's 200-degree full/rear-hemisphere field.
The output is a flat four-coefficient fisheye profile directly accepted by wideangle_mapping_audit.py and stereo_fisheye_calibrate.py. It never permits hardware programming by itself.
